name: Auguste Comte
role: French philosopher and founder of positivism and sociology (1798-1857)
summary: Comte sought to end the disorder of the post-revolutionary West by a science of society and a secular Religion of Humanity. He favoured a provisional progressive dictatorship with free speech, separation of an advisory priesthood from temporal power, small republics, a disbanded army and an end to colonial rule. He opposed popular sovereignty, equal rights and Communism, and wanted women kept in the family and property left in private hands under moral control.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: he opposes economists who think industry needs no organisation, yet entrusts industry to private chiefs and not the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Rejects the Communist solution of changing the tenure of property; control should be moral and legal tenure left alone.

unions-good.rationale: He proposes authorising workers' coalitions as fully as employers' as useful preparation for the normal state, under priestly arbitration.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mixed: he forbids legal interference with property and defends inheritance, but denies the notion of rights and says property is social and morally controlled.

worker-ownership.rationale: Says property should stay with industrial chiefs, who act on their own responsibility, and that Communism is worthless as a system.

strong-leader.rationale: In 1848 he proposed a provisional revolutionary dictatorship: a three-man central executive that convokes and dissolves the electoral body, with an assembly cut to about 200 members who only vote the budget. The 1850s volume again supports a progressive dictatorial government.

state-harmful.rationale: He treats a strong central government as necessary for order and says that even in the normal state government must repress the more dangerous delinquencies by force.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: the 1848 text sides with the central power over the local in almost all cases, while the later works break large states into small republics of one to three million people.

traditional-family.rationale: Treats the family as the natural element of society and the primal basis of moral life; the 1848 text calls its preservation of great importance and requires exclusive, indissoluble monogamy.

more-religion-public.rationale: He builds a public religion of Humanity with temples, festivals, sacraments and a priesthood that guides public life.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Says sex differences follow natural law: man surpasses woman in force, as throughout the animal kingdom, and the sexes tend to differentiate, not converge.

gradual-change.rationale: Mixed: he warns against political reconstruction before moral reform and against upsetting society over abuses already being removed, yet proposes abolishing the army, the parliamentary regime and large states.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Contested: he prizes science and machinery but says social ills need a remedy 'almost entirely of a moral kind'.

revolution-justified.rationale: Says insurrection is an ultimate resource no society should do without and that Positivism would sanction and even encourage it when really indispensable.

experts-over-public.rationale: Says it would be absurd to ask the people to judge cases where it is incompetent, such as scientific enactments and special trades, and that it should adopt the view of superior officers; he also says philosophers give counsel and capitalists give direction.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: he leaves industry to private chiefs under moral regulation and calls the Communist solution chimerical.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Defends inheritance as the means by which each generation hands on its work; calls condemnation of it narrow and subversive, and allows freedom of bequest.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Capital is concentrated in a few patricians, whose task is to direct its employment; the state is limited to material order.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mixed: he wants capital concentrated in a patriciate and small capitalists absorbed, but wants every proletarian family to own its dwelling and daily possessions.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He keeps wages, split into a fixed part and one varying with results, but treats labour as gratuitous and wages as replacing materials consumed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In 1848 he called abolition of monarchy the one irrevocable political point, a symbol of retrogression; later he spoke respectfully of a Russian autocrat guiding reform, so evidence is mixed.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejects the 'sovereignty of the people' as a metaphysical dogma useful only for demolition, says the people are fit to rule only in exceptional cases, and calls choice of superiors by inferiors anarchical.

direct-votes.rationale: He holds that the people should not decide political questions or choose rulers; their role is to form public opinion, and on technical measures they should adopt the view of qualified officers.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejects political supremacy of the people and proposes parliament be cut down and replaced by a three-man executive; no council system appears.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Catechism expects and welcomes the peaceful, voluntary breakup of large states (France into seventeen republics, Ireland leaving England) because a state is free only if its parts join of their own will.

political-violence-never.rationale: In 1848 he accepts insurrection as a last resort against tyranny, though the Catechism condemns recourse to arms between classes.

war-builds-character.rationale: Says the conquest of Algeria was meant to cultivate a ferocious temper and corrupt the French nation; he wants industrial peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mixed: spiritual and temporal powers are separate, with no state grants to churches in 1848, but the later Catechism has the Positive priesthood paid from the state treasury.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Positive polity is founded on demonstrated science and a morality of Humanity, 'irrespectively of God'.

military-superiority.rationale: France should abandon precautions against neighbours by suppressing its army so that other states' establishments fall.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He treats intellectual evolution through three stages as the driver of social development and class conflict as a pathology to be mediated.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rejects absolute equality: classification is necessary, and men beyond the right to develop their activity are not equal or equivalent.

civilizational-union.rationale: For the Western republics he says their union will be religious, not political; sixty independent republics will share only education, customs and festivals.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His formula is 'live for others'; he treats egoism as the natural disorder to be reversed by teaching altruism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He wants the word right removed from political language: 'no one has any Right but that of doing his Duty', with duties towards all.

limit-population.rationale: Says regulation of growth in population is required, to be achieved morally and voluntarily, never by legal checks.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Calls industrialism most favourable to social life and expects it to replace the military character.

restore-past-order.rationale: He condemns the retrograde party and says order and progress must be reconciled; he admires the medieval separation of powers but does not seek to restore the old order.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: His 1848 provisional dictatorship would be staffed by working men, whom he judged best qualified for political power in the transition; however it places no check on capitalists and is not directed against a former ruling class.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He expects industrial society to replace military life and ensure permanent peace.

conscription.rationale: Proposes suppressing the French army for a voluntary gendarmerie, noting compulsory enlistment has never been needed there.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He attributes distinct mental qualities to the three typical races as differences of organisation: the Black race above the White in feeling and below it in intellect, the Yellow in activity.

total-state.rationale: He limits the temporal government to material questions and public order, and assigns education, morals and opinion to an independent spiritual power that only counsels; he warns against tyrannical interference by the state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Calls the conquest of Algeria an act of oppression, wants a thoroughly pacific policy, and condemns the extension of military empire.

universal-morality.rationale: He proposes a positive morality demonstrable by science and valid for all peoples, and says the laws of development apply to all climates and races.

single-common-good.rationale: Holds that all forces should work for the common good, which a recognised code of principles must determine, and that politics balancing local against central power is mistaken.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Calls the choice of the superior by the inferior thoroughly anarchical; industrial chiefs act under their own moral responsibility and are subject to no control.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mixed: he calls national independence a provisional metaphysical dogma, but wants small states whose parts join freely.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He says the intellect must be the servant of the heart, never its slave, and that affection preponderates in action, while demanding that knowledge rest on observation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wants the philosophic body to act as arbitrator between workers and employers, and says the strong owe devotion and the weak veneration.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Holds that women should be kept out of political authority and industry and concentrated in family life, but says this should become law only after becoming custom.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He says the natural arrangements of society are far less faulty than the claims of women's champions suggest, and treats women's position as a privilege.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rejects prohibiting marriage to those of bad constitution as oppressive and illusory; prefers voluntary moral regulation of births.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mixed: in the transition he limits government almost entirely to maintaining material order, but he also has the state pay priests, fund Positive schools and guarantee support for women without husbands.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He says men are not equal, can have no identical rights beyond the original one, and that the dogma of equality is anarchic once taken as absolute.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mixed: he rejects popular sovereignty and election of rulers, yet says no lasting social change is legitimate without the voluntary assent of the classes involved.

separated-powers.rationale: He calls the balancing of legislative against executive an empirical error, and says a system of checks and complications ends in irresponsibility; he separates spiritual from temporal power instead.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1848 text says well-being of the people should be the one great object of government and the strong owe devotion to the weak.

party-controls-media.rationale: He demands perfect liberty of speech and discussion, abolition of penalties and fines on the press, and says even the priesthood must not suppress contrary opinions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Mixed: his Western Republic is a union of small republics bound by common education and worship, which he says will be 'religious, not political', though he proposes common coinage, a fleet and a committee for the West.

clerical-rule.rationale: His priesthood must renounce all temporal power and property and only counsel; the supreme temporal power belongs to three bankers.

people-in-arms.rationale: Wants the national guard suppressed as a force at variance with modern feeling and a danger to order.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Says the white race is superior to the other two, that other nations are inferior in development, and that Western Europe leads under France.

death-penalty.rationale: Says capital punishment will never be wholly disused, that abolishing it is contrary to laws of human nature, and that society must remove irredeemable offenders.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is a public trust and a social function: private property should be turned into a public function without legal interference.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Spiritual power must be wholly independent of temporal power, so he rejects state control of the clergy, though he would end grants to theological bodies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He wants factitious aggregates dissolved by peaceful means and says free states are formed without violence; he does not endorse force to hold regions in.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Says 'ideas govern the world or throw it into chaos' and that all social mechanism rests on opinions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women should abstain from practical authority and public office; a woman's life belongs to the family, though six women would sit on his proposed Council.

moral-incentives.rationale: Says wages replace materials consumed, not pay merit; the priesthood would set up an abstract classification by merit and honour to counterbalance rank.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Contested: he urges wise Western intervention on behalf of less advanced peoples as a moral mission, but denounces Algeria as an act of oppression and rejects military empire.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Catechism says election was only a protest against caste and that 'the choice of the superior by the inferior is thoroughly anarchical'; each functionary names his successor, subject to approval from above.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He argues that absolute submission would expose us to tyranny and keeps insurrection in reserve for extreme cases.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He wanted the legislature reduced to about 200 members voting only the budget, with all executive and legislative measures in the central power's hands, and later welcomed the abolition of the parliamentary regime.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Catechism sets 'devotion of the strong to the weak' as a social maxim and reminds the patriciate of its eternal duties to the proletariat.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage must be 'exclusive and indissoluble'; he criticises Protestant divorce laws and says love needs a check on caprice.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: he says no society can last if inferiors do not respect superiors and treats subordination as the rule, with revolt only in exceptional cases.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Says the intervention of society in marriage is necessary to confirm and develop the natural order, making the union exclusive and indissoluble.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mixed: he treats theological belief as a passing stage that Positivism supersedes, but holds religion itself is a permanent human need.

socialized-care.rationale: Education of children belongs to mothers at home until puberty; he treats women's life as domestic and calls alms-houses and foundling hospitals Communist institutions that popular feeling rightly condemns.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejects Communism as a system and the economists' view that industry needs no organisation; he proposes moral control of property by the priesthood and public opinion.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: he wants all penalties hampering discussion abolished and full freedom to criticise doctrines.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Calls for restoring Algeria to the Arabs as an act of justice, saying the colony rests on iniquity and is incompatible with reorganising society.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He says the people are not fit for political supremacy; their function is to assist the spiritual power in forming public opinion, not to govern.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He seeks the 'entire reconcilement' of Order and Progress, denouncing both the retrograde and the anarchic schools.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He says Western ideas of the difference between Eastern and Western manners are exaggerated and that Islamic peoples will look to Positivism for guidance.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: His 1848 motto is 'reorganisation irrespectively of God or king': authority rests on Humanity, not God or the people.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He proposes definitively suppressing the army, leaving a constabulary plus a reduced artillery and navy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He calls large fortunes eminently desirable and wants capital concentrated in few patrician hands.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He says he repudiated any connection between Positivism and atheism, calling atheism an imperfect emancipation that keeps theological problems alive.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: he wants poverty addressed by moral agencies and the duty of patricians rather than by legislation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: He says women should not govern or exercise practical authority and calls public life wisely forbidden to them; his priesthood is composed of men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He says in the family woman's influence is that of persuasion rather than command, and that man must provide for and command practical life.

family-wage.rationale: Says man should provide for woman and that this will shape wages; wages should replace the materials consumed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Calls women the affective element, superior to men in social feeling and in placing social above personal feeling.

arms-reduction.rationale: Proposes replacing the French army with about eighty thousand gendarmes, with artillery and navy cut to a quarter.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: he would leave only a state gendarmerie and constabulary and suppress the national guard.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: States that women should not be allowed to inherit; capital should revert to men, though not by law until custom establishes it.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: he requires exclusive, indissoluble monogamy and condemns 'levity and inconsistency in love'.

women-suffrage.rationale: Says women's qualities do not involve political power, that they are excluded from every kind of political authority, and that their role is to modify, not govern.

race-social-construct.rationale: Holds that three races present really positive distinctions of organisation, though they will be harmonised as civilisation advances.

national-church-status.rationale: Says it would be retrogression to give legal sanction to any old creed and wants all grants to theological and metaphysical bodies ended.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: he opposes conscription altogether, so the 'neither' option of the statement matches.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Holds marriage indissoluble, and in the Catechism requires eternal widowhood, so no spouse can end it unilaterally.

notes: Quotes come from English translations (Bridges, Congreve, Martineau, Congreve's Polity). The 1848 General View favours a strong central power; later volumes (cited by the Stanford Encyclopedia) place temporal power in small local republics, so decide-locally is mixed. His most recent position (1850s) is used for the priesthood's state funding and for the abolition of parliament. Inheritance, women and race answers follow his own statements.
